findings.reason: 'tildes' is the colloquial word for the acute accent; strictly ü, ç, à are also refused by the ASCII grammar. The common Spanish cases (á é í ó ú ñ) are named, so it reads natively and is accurate in practice. Acceptable as is.
English has the same Key-label vs 'name' wording; es faithfully follows en and shipped 'Un nombre corto para la línea de trabajo'. Not counted; noted for the source owner.
